bibl.title: Inhibition-induced theta resonance in cortical circuits

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: whether the theta-band resonance seen in the membrane potential in vitro appears in the spiking of the same cells in a behaving animal
span.quote: In vitro, pyramidal cells exhibit theta-band membrane potential (subthreshold) resonance, but whether and how sub-threshold resonance translates into spiking resonance in behaving animals is unknown.

span.label: whether and how subthreshold resonance is translated to the spiking regime in behaving animals
span.quote: Yet, it is not clear if and how subthreshold resonance is translated to the suprathreshold (spiking) regime ( Magee, 1998 ; Pike at all., 2000 ; Ulrich, 2002 ; Richardson et al., 2003 ) in behaving animals.

span.label: spiking resonance at theta is not intrinsic to the pyramidal cell but is conferred on it by rhythmic PV inhibition, and it requires HCN currents
span.quote: Thus, PV interneurons mediate pyramidal cell spiking resonance in intact cortical networks, favoring transmission at theta frequency.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: Thus, PV interneurons mediate pyramidal cell spiking resonance in intact cortical networks, favoring transmission at theta frequency.

span.label: theta-band spiking resonance in cortical pyramidal cells
span.quote: In vitro, pyramidal cells exhibit theta-band membrane potential (subthreshold) resonance, but whether and how sub-threshold resonance translates into spiking resonance in behaving animals is unknown.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: Using large scale extracellular recordings and optogenetics in freely-behaving mice, we showed that wide-band periodic but not random noise activation of PV interneurons induces theta frequency-favored spiking in hippocampal and neocortical pyramidal cells accompanied by post-inhibitory rebound spiking.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: periodic PV inhibition hyperpolarizes pyramidal cells, activating HCN/Ih channels whose deinactivation produces time-locked post-inhibitory rebound spikes at theta frequency
span.quote: Although several mechanisms might account for the theta band spiking resonance ( Hu et al., 2002 ), our experiments suggest that to a large part, the effect is mediated by the activation of HCN channels in pyramidal cells, since pharmacological blockade of HCN channels largely abolished theta-band spiking resonance.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: rebound spiking of a fixed latency after release from inhibition acts as a band-pass filter on the inhibitory input frequency
span.quote: Second, active properties of pyramidal cells ( Hu et al., 2002 ; Stuart et al., 2007 ) may induce time-locked rebound spiking upon recovery from inhibition ( Llinas et al., 1982 ; Cobb et al., 1995 ) of specific duration, creating in effect a band-pass filter.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: at high input frequencies dense PV spiking tonically suppresses targets while at low frequencies gaps in inhibition let pyramidal cells fire, which alone acts as a low-pass filter
span.quote: First, at high frequencies the high density of spikes emitted by PV cells can tonically suppress their targets, whereas at lower frequencies PYR can still fire in longer windows devoid of strong PV activity, creating in effect a low-pass filter.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: short-term depression of the inhibitory synapse weakens hyperpolarization at low input frequencies, removing the drive for Ih activation and so suppressing sub-theta rebound
span.quote: Following intense presynaptic INT spiking, the inhibitory synapses on the PYR are less activated, so the hyperpolarization drive to I h activation is reduced.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: PV interneurons of the active assembly suppress competing cells, and release from that inhibition triggers rebound spikes that seed the next cell assembly on the opposite theta phase
span.quote: We hypothesize that the rebound spikes, induced by release from PV interneuron-mediated inhibition, contribute to the initiation of runner-up assemblies.

span.label: the inductive effects of the hyperpolarization-activated current create a negative feedback that opposes voltage changes, and that feedback is what creates resonance
span.quote: The inductive effects of I h create a negative feedback that opposes the voltage changes and thus creates resonance

span.label: a low-pass account is available too: dense PV spiking tonically suppresses targets at high frequencies while low frequencies leave windows in which pyramidal cells can still fire
span.quote: Theta band-limited discharge of PYR upon PV neuron activation can occur for at least two reasons. First, at high frequencies the high density of spikes emitted by PV cells can tonically suppress their targets, whereas at lower frequencies PYR can still fire in longer windows devoid of strong PV activity, creating in effect a low-pass filter. This scenario is compatible with the frequency filtering properties of inhibitory synapses ( Thomson et al., 2002 ; Markram et al., 2004 ). Second, active properties of pyramidal cells ( Hu et al., 2002 ; Stuart et al., 2007 ) may induce time-locked rebound spiking upon recovery from inhibition ( Llinas et al., 1982 ; Cobb et al., 1995 ) of specific duration, creating in effect a band-pass filter.

span.label: HCN alone gives rebound at sub-theta frequencies as well, so a timing mechanism is needed to suppress the low end and turn a low-pass into a band-pass
span.quote: When the PYR model included I h , INT activation in the low frequency range induced rebound PYR spiking ( Figure 8A ). However, this range included sub-theta frequencies. Theta-band spiking regime resonance was especially robust when the model included a timing mechanism that prevented the generation of action potentials at low frequencies, implemented by either network-mediated timed inhibition

span.label: an OLM interneuron released from inhibition just in time can block the low-frequency rebound, which is one way to implement that timing mechanism
span.quote: During low-frequency INT stimulation, the OLM cell was inhibited by the INT and released from inhibition “just in time” to inhibit PYR and prevent post-inhibitory rebound during the high stimulus phase, in effect creating a PYR spiking band-pass filter.

span.label: depression of the inhibitory synapses is the other way: at low input frequencies the presynaptic rate is higher, the synapses depress, and the hyperpolarisation that would drive HCN is reduced
span.quote: Following intense presynaptic INT spiking, the inhibitory synapses on the PYR are less activated, so the hyperpolarization drive to I h activation is reduced. Synaptic depression is more effective at lower input frequencies where the pre-synaptic input spiking is higher. Thus, at low stimulation frequencies, post-inhibitory rebound spiking is not generated, resulting in theta-range resonant spiking.

span.label: PV cells themselves show no frequency preference, which is consistent with basket cells lacking the current that produces it
span.quote: Individual locally-recorded PV cells reliably followed the alternating light patterns up to 40 Hz but showed no particular frequency preference, consistent with the lack of I h in basket cells

span.label: The pharmacological result shows Ih is necessary but not sufficient for theta spiking resonance
span.quote: The pharmacological experiments established the requirement of I h for theta-band spiking resonance but not its sufficiency.

span.label: HCN channels are not the whole story; further mechanisms may sharpen the resonance in intact networks
span.quote: Whereas previous in vitro and the present in vivo experiments provide strong support for a critical role of HCN channels in theta band resonance and excess rebound spiking of pyramidal cells following periodic inhibition, additional mechanisms ( Figure 8B,C ) may sharpen PYR spiking resonance in the intact network.

span.label: The proposed assembly-seeding function of rebound spikes is acknowledged as speculative
span.quote: While speculative, this hypothesis is compatible with all known observations on putative basket neurons ( Klausberger and Somogyi, 2008 ) and their temporal relationship with pyramidal cells, including the present observations.

span.label: the blockade establishes that HCN is required and explicitly not that it is sufficient
span.quote: The pharmacological experiments established the requirement of I h for theta-band spiking resonance but not its sufficiency. To investigate whether I h alone is sufficient, we constructed a biophysical model of mutually-connected PYR and INT with active currents driven by a chirp pattern current to the INT.

span.label: further mechanisms beyond HCN are expected to sharpen the resonance in the intact network
span.quote: Whereas previous in vitro and the present in vivo experiments provide strong support for a critical role of HCN channels in theta band resonance and excess rebound spiking of pyramidal cells following periodic inhibition, additional mechanisms ( Figure 8B,C ) may sharpen PYR spiking resonance in the intact network.

span.label: the assembly-seeding account of the rebound spikes is labelled speculative by the authors
span.quote: While speculative, this hypothesis is compatible with all known observations on putative basket neurons ( Klausberger and Somogyi, 2008 ) and their temporal relationship with pyramidal cells, including the present observations.

span.label: a gain-baseline correlation is offered with its own artefactual reading, a spiking rate ceiling
span.quote: During PV chirp-pattern activation, frequency-independent PYR spiking gain was negatively correlated with baseline rate (rank correlation, −0.31; n=110 PYR; p<0.001, permutation test; Figure S5A ), presumably due to a spiking rate ceiling effect.

span.label: a coherence-baseline correlation is likewise offered as possibly a floor effect, since silent cells cannot be suppressed further
span.quote: PYR with higher baseline rates were also more coherent with the PV chirp stimulus (rank correlation, 0.31; p=0.003; Figure S5B ). This increased coherence may simply be a floor effect as silent cells cannot be suppressed further.

span.label: the number of interneurons actually illuminated is an estimate spanning an order of magnitude
span.quote: The weak focal photostimulation affected an estimated 2–20 PV interneurons (depending on light intensity and cell density; Royer et al., 2012; Stark et al., 2012 ), and did not affect the frequency or phase of the global theta rhythm

span.label: half the recorded units were classified by waveform rather than by tagging, and low-confidence ones were dropped
span.quote: Non-tagged units (692 of 1413, 51%) are classified as putative pyramidal cells (PYR) or interneurons (INT) according to waveform morphology; non-tagged units with low classification confidence (p>0.05, n=22, 1.6%) are not analyzed

span.label: the chirp - a linear frequency sweep - used as a stimulus to read a biological system's frequency response
span.quote: In principle, part of the frequency preference of individual cells could result from slow adaptation (due to e.g., ChR2 dynamics, cellular adaptation, and/or calcium buildup). To examine this possibility we tested a subset of units with both ascending (0–40 Hz) and descending (40-0 Hz) chirps

span.label: low-pass filter and band-pass filter as the names for the two candidate explanations of the same band-limited discharge
span.quote: Theta band-limited discharge of PYR upon PV neuron activation can occur for at least two reasons. First, at high frequencies the high density of spikes emitted by PV cells can tonically suppress their targets, whereas at lower frequencies PYR can still fire in longer windows devoid of strong PV activity, creating in effect a low-pass filter. This scenario is compatible with the frequency filtering properties of inhibitory synapses ( Thomson et al., 2002 ; Markram et al., 2004 ). Second, active properties of pyramidal cells ( Hu et al., 2002 ; Stuart et al., 2007 ) may induce time-locked rebound spiking upon recovery from inhibition ( Llinas et al., 1982 ; Cobb et al., 1995 ) of specific duration, creating in effect a band-pass filter.

span.label: resonance here is defined generically as amplification in a limited frequency band, which is what lets the same word cover a membrane potential effect and a spiking effect that this paper shows come apart
span.quote: In general, resonance refers to an amplifying mechanism in a limited frequency band

span.label: subthreshold and suprathreshold resonance are separate claims: the first is established in vitro, the second is what this paper asks about, and directly-driven pyramidal cells do NOT show the second
span.quote: In vitro, pyramidal cells exhibit theta-band membrane potential (subthreshold) resonance, but whether and how sub-threshold resonance translates into spiking resonance in behaving animals is unknown.

span.label: INT is defined by a NEGATIVE result - interneurons NOT driven by the light - so the class is an outcome of the manipulation rather than a cell type, and the authors say some of them are probably PV cells that the light missed
span.quote: The abbreviation INT refers to physiologically identified putative interneurons that were not driven during PV photostimulation (a subset of INT may be PV cells which were not activated by light).

span.label: the opsin's specificity and sensitivity are measured separately: every labelled cell was PV, but 10 percent of PV cells were unlabelled
span.quote: In five PV-cre::Ai32 animals, all 84 EYFP+ cells were PV+ (100%) and 84 of 93 PV+ cells were EYFP+ (90%).

span.label: a well-isolated unit is defined by three explicit numerical thresholds on amplitude, cluster quality and refractory violations
span.quote: Only well-isolated units (amplitude > 50 μV; L-ratio < 0.05, Schmitzer-Torbert et al. 2005 ; ISI index < 0.2, Fee et al. 1996 ) were considered.

span.label: the theta index is a ratio to the cell's own broadband coherence, so it equals 1 under no bias - the measure carries its own null
span.quote: To quantify theta-band preference, we calculated a “theta-index” for each cell (mean theta-band coherence divided by the 0–40 Hz coherence), which is equal to 1 when there is no bias.

span.label: the ZD-index is a normalised difference between control and drug coherence, built so that the drug effect can be shown to be specific to a frequency band and a cell type rather than global
span.quote: To further quantify the frequency-specificity of the drug effect for each unit, a “ZD-index” was computed ( Figure 7C , right), defined as the difference between the control and drug-effect coherence divided by the sum. This measure was selectively high for PYR at theta-band frequency

span.label: builds-on → Zemankovics et al., 2010 (lack of Ih in basket cells)
span.quote: Individual locally-recorded PV cells reliably followed the alternating light patterns up to 40 Hz but showed no particular frequency preference, consistent with the lack of I h in basket cells ( Zemankovics et al., 2010 ).

span.label: replicates → Stark et al., 2012 (local activation by the light cone of diode-probes)
span.quote: During single-shank chirp pattern PV activation, non-local units were weakly activated or not activated, similar to DC pulses ( Figure 1C ) and confirming previous demonstrations of local activation by the light cone ( Stark et al., 2012 ).

span.label: qualifies → the in vitro finding of theta-band subthreshold resonance in cortical principal neurons under intracellular sinusoidal injection
span.quote: The in vitro tests typically examined resonance by intracellular current injection of a chirp pattern at a hyperpolarized membrane potential while synaptic activity was blocked pharmacologically. The difference between the in vivo and in vitro results can be explained by the presence of synaptic activity in vivo and/or the depolarizing effect of the light-induced chirp in our experiments.

span.label: builds-on → Cobb 1995's demonstration that basket cell burst discharge induces rebound spikes after release from hyperpolarization in vitro
span.quote: The inductive effects of I h create a negative feedback that opposes the voltage changes and thus creates resonance

span.label: extends → the account of theta generation as a consortium of septal pacemaker, circuit interactions and intrinsic neuronal properties
span.quote: In summary, our experiments uncovered an inhibition-based component of theta-band spiking resonance, which may affect the frequency-dependence of spiking in the hippocampus and neocortex. The circuit properties described herein enable preferential transmission of theta-frequency activity to target populations, post-synaptic to theta-oscillating interneurons, and may amplify theta-range spiking in local circuits.

span.label: supports → an HCN-mediated mechanism for post-hyperpolarization rebound spiking
span.quote: In contrast, during and after I h blocker infusion, theta band preference of PYR spiking was abolished at the population (p=0.014, U -test comparing peak frequencies during control and drug-effect periods; PV, p=0.74; Figure 7A and Figure 7B ) and at the single-unit level (p<0.001, Wilcoxon’s paired signed rank test comparing theta indices during control and drug-effect periods; PV, p=0.22

span.label: critiques → the use of grand averages to describe the relationship between pyramidal cells and perisomatic interneurons
span.quote: Yet, grand averages do not correctly describe the dynamic relationship between pyramidal cells and perisomatic interneurons.

span.label: subthreshold resonance —distinct-from→ spiking resonance
span.quote: Thus, PYR subthreshold resonance was not communicated to the spiking regime even at low levels of CaMKII activation; instead, PYR spiking resonance increased with the level of PV activation (inhibition).

span.label: PV —causes→ spiking resonance
span.quote: Thus, PV interneurons mediate pyramidal cell spiking resonance in intact cortical networks, favoring transmission at theta frequency.

span.label: PV —distinct-from→ INT
span.quote: The abbreviation INT refers to physiologically identified putative interneurons that were not driven during PV photostimulation (a subset of INT may be PV cells which were not activated by light).

span.label: I h —causes→ resonance
span.quote: The inductive effects of I h create a negative feedback that opposes the voltage changes and thus creates resonance

span.label: ZD7288 —operationalised-as→ HCN1
span.quote: To test the hypothesized role of I h , we infused a specific HCN1 channel blocker (ZD7288; Gasparini and DiFrancesco, 1997 ; Hu et al., 2002 ) into the CA1 radiatum/lacunosum-moleculare of urethane-anesthetized PV::ChR2 mice (n=5) during chirp pattern photostimulation.

span.label: ZD-index —operationalised-as→ PYR
span.quote: To further quantify the frequency-specificity of the drug effect for each unit, a “ZD-index” was computed ( Figure 7C , right), defined as the difference between the control and drug-effect coherence divided by the sum. This measure was selectively high for PYR at theta-band frequency

span.label: HCN1 —part-of→ CA1
span.quote: HCN1 channels are especially abundant in the distal apical dendrites of CA1 and neocortical layer 5 pyramidal cells

span.label: chirp —contrasted-with→ white-noise
span.quote: we compared the response to chirp and filtered white-noise (WN; generated by convolving uncorrelated WN with a 3 ms exponential; Figure 4Aa ) stimuli in a subset of cells

span.label: frequency correlation —contrasted-with→ time correlation
span.quote: To quantify the frequency/time preference of individual units, we computed, for each cell, two rank correlation coefficients (“frequency correlation” and “time correlation”) between the coherences under the two conditions. For a pure frequency-dependent unit, the coherences during ascending and descending chirps should be identical, and the rank correlation between them (“frequency correlation”) is 1. In contrast, for a pure time-dependent unit the coherences should be mirror images (assuming phase is preserved) and thus the rank correlation between the ascending chirp coherence and the reversed descending chirp coherence is 1.

span.label: adaptation —distinct-from→ chirp
span.quote: In principle, part of the frequency preference of individual cells could result from slow adaptation (due to e.g., ChR2 dynamics, cellular adaptation, and/or calcium buildup). To examine this possibility we tested a subset of units with both ascending (0–40 Hz) and descending (40-0 Hz) chirps

span.label: band-pass filter —contrasted-with→ low-pass filter
span.quote: Theta band-limited discharge of PYR upon PV neuron activation can occur for at least two reasons. First, at high frequencies the high density of spikes emitted by PV cells can tonically suppress their targets, whereas at lower frequencies PYR can still fire in longer windows devoid of strong PV activity, creating in effect a low-pass filter. This scenario is compatible with the frequency filtering properties of inhibitory synapses ( Thomson et al., 2002 ; Markram et al., 2004 ). Second, active properties of pyramidal cells ( Hu et al., 2002 ; Stuart et al., 2007 ) may induce time-locked rebound spiking upon recovery from inhibition ( Llinas et al., 1982 ; Cobb et al., 1995 ) of specific duration, creating in effect a band-pass filter.

span.label: OLM —causes→ band-pass filter
span.quote: During low-frequency INT stimulation, the OLM cell was inhibited by the INT and released from inhibition “just in time” to inhibit PYR and prevent post-inhibitory rebound during the high stimulus phase, in effect creating a PYR spiking band-pass filter.

span.label: synaptic depression —causes→ I h
span.quote: Following intense presynaptic INT spiking, the inhibitory synapses on the PYR are less activated, so the hyperpolarization drive to I h activation is reduced. Synaptic depression is more effective at lower input frequencies where the pre-synaptic input spiking is higher. Thus, at low stimulation frequencies, post-inhibitory rebound spiking is not generated, resulting in theta-range resonant spiking.

span.quote: Overall, 50/110 (45%) of the light-modulated PYR rebounded at the chirp pattern theta trough, with a median gain of 3.2 (range, 1.2–25

span.quote: To quantify theta-band preference, we calculated a “theta-index” for each cell (mean theta-band coherence divided by the 0–40 Hz coherence), which is equal to 1 when there is no bias.

span.label: RETRACTED (THE NOTE AND THE TYPE SAY OPPOSITE THINGS) · CA1 —contrasted-with→ neocortical
span.quote: The proportions and effect sizes were similar among neocortical and CA1 PYR (p=0.97, χ 2 test; and p=0.91, Mann-Whitney U-test

span.label: diode-probe —operationalised-as→ PV
span.quote: Waveforms of the pyramidal cell (PYR) and interneuron (PV) at the 8 sites of the diode-probe shank (20 μm spacing) during PV activation and spontaneous activity

span.label: Kolmogorov-Smirnov test
span.quote: The significant coherence between the light stimulus and spiking was predominantly at the theta frequency band (4–11 Hz; Figure 2C , top right; p<0.001, Kolmogorov-Smirnov test with a uniform null; Figure S2B ).

span.label: permutation test
span.quote: The mean±SEM frequency correlation was 0.19±0.04 and 0.32±0.04 for CaMKII and PV animals, respectively (p<0.001 for both, permutation test with a zero correlation null), whereas the time correlation was 0.054±0.04 and 0.02±0.05 (p=0.02 and p=0.6; Figure 4E ).

span.label: chi-squared test
span.quote: The proportions and effect sizes were similar among neocortical and CA1 PYR (p=0.97, χ 2 test; and p=0.91, Mann-Whitney U-test; Figure 3Bc ; Figure S3 ).

span.label: Mann-Whitney U test
span.quote: The proportions and effect sizes were similar among neocortical and CA1 PYR (p=0.97, χ 2 test; and p=0.91, Mann-Whitney U-test; Figure 3Bc ; Figure S3 ).

span.label: Kruskal-Wallis test
span.quote: Theta indices were highest for PYR during PV activation (p<0.05, Kruskal-Wallis test corrected for multiple comparisons; Figure 2D ).

span.label: Wilcoxon signed-rank test
span.quote: Following ZD7288 infusion, local field activity and PYR spiking rates were slightly reduced (LFP: p<0.05, Bonferroni-corrected paired t-test; Figure S7A ; PYR spiking: p=0.011, Wilcoxon’s paired signed-rank test; Figure S7B )

span.label: t-test
span.quote: Following ZD7288 infusion, local field activity and PYR spiking rates were slightly reduced (LFP: p<0.05, Bonferroni-corrected paired t-test; Figure S7A ; PYR spiking: p=0.011, Wilcoxon’s paired signed-rank test; Figure S7B )

span.label: rank correlation
span.quote: Local INT theta peak gain predicted chirp-spiking coherence in concurrently-recorded PYR: the rank correlation was 0.3 for light-modulated PYR (p<0.001, permutation test) and 0.52 for all PYR (p<0.001; Figure S5E ).

span.label: Poisson test
span.quote: At the “optimal” intensity (activating the largest number of targeted units per shank), 33% (101/309) of locally-stimulated PYR were activated (p<0.05; Poisson test) in CaMKII::ChR2 mice, whereas in PV::ChR2 animals, 59% (108/184) of locally-stimulated interneurons were activated

span.label: Rayleigh test
span.quote: Middle panels, spiking gain maps of CA1 units during LFP theta; only theta-band modulated units are included (p<0.05, Rayleigh test).

span.label: binomial test
span.quote: Blue bars indicate phase bins for which the number of units with increased spiking (gain>1) exceeds chance level (exact Binomial test, p<0.001).

span.label: spectral coherence (multi-taper estimate)
span.quote: For each unit recorded during linear chirp stimulation, the multi-taper coherence and phase were estimated between the current driving the diode and the raw spike train (both digitized at 1250 Hz).

span.label: standard error of the mean
span.quote: Chirp-pattern photostimulation of PV interneurons often induced high firing rates (mean±SEM 142±13 spikes/sec, n=52 frequency modulated PV; Figure S2D )

span.quote: Similarly to the observations in the freely-moving animals, during chirp-pattern activation of PV neurons, PYR spiked predominantly during stimulus troughs (linear phase model: Φ(f)=(π+0.12)+0.06f; R 2 =0.87) of the theta band (peak frequency, 9.8±0.9 Hz; p<0.001, Kolmogorov-Smirnov test comparing to a uniform distribution; Figure 7B , top ).

span.label: permutation test
span.quote: This again was not due to inefficient suppression since WN-induced PYR spiking gains were similar, on a cell-by-cell basis, to chirp induced suppression (rank correlation between spiking gains of 100 PYR modulated by either stimulus was 0.58; p<0.001, permutation test).

span.label: Kolmogorov-Smirnov test
span.quote: The significant coherence between the light stimulus and spiking was predominantly at the theta frequency band (4–11 Hz; Figure 2C , top right; p<0.001, Kolmogorov-Smirnov test with a uniform null

span.quote: During PV chirp-pattern activation, frequency-independent PYR spiking gain was negatively correlated with baseline rate (rank correlation, −0.31; n=110 PYR; p<0.001, permutation test; Figure S5A ), presumably due to a spiking rate ceiling effect.

span.label: U-test
span.quote: In fact, WN-pattern PV-activation suppressed spiking more strongly than the chirp-pattern (PYR gain during chirp: 0.49±0.09, and WN: 0.28±0.07; n=100 PYR; p<0.001, U-test

span.label: Directly photoactivated pyramidal cells each spiked in a narrow frequency band, but the preferred band differed between cells and across the population covered the whole 0-40 Hz range, i.e. no group-level theta preference.
span.quote: Although individual PYR tended to spike at narrow frequency bands, this band differed from cell to cell and, at the group level, spanned the entire range of tested frequencies (p=0.44; Kolmogorov-Smirnov test with a uniform null; Figure 2C , left ; Figure S2B ).

span.label: When PV interneurons rather than pyramidal cells were driven with the chirp, pyramidal-cell spiking became coherent with the stimulus specifically in the 4-11 Hz theta band.
span.quote: The significant coherence between the light stimulus and spiking was predominantly at the theta frequency band (4–11 Hz; Figure 2C , top right; p<0.001, Kolmogorov-Smirnov test with a uniform null; Figure S2B ).

span.label: Nearly half of the light-modulated pyramidal cells fired excess rebound spikes at the trough of the theta-band chirp, with a median firing-rate gain of 3.2 over baseline.
span.quote: Overall, 50/110 (45%) of the light-modulated PYR rebounded at the chirp pattern theta trough, with a median gain of 3.2 (range, 1.2–25; Figure 3Bc ).

span.label: White-noise PV activation suppressed pyramidal cells even more strongly than the chirp yet produced almost no frequency-modulated pyramidal spiking (2 of 271 cells), showing that rhythmic rather than merely strong inhibition is what creates resonance.
span.quote: Despite strong activation of PV neurons ( Figure 4B ), the WN-induced inhibition did not induce phase-locked spiking in PYR as only 0.7% (2/271) PYR were significantly frequency modulated.

span.label: Cells kept the same frequency preference whether the chirp ascended 0-40 Hz or descended 40-0 Hz, ruling out slow adaptation as the cause of the resonance.
span.quote: In summary, resonant spiking of PYR upon PV activation does not result from adaptation processes, and a rhythmic pattern of inhibition is required for inhibition-induced resonant PYR spiking.

span.label: The stronger the local inhibitory drive, measured as the theta peak gain of the interneuron on the same shank, the more theta-coherent and phase-concentrated the pyramidal cell's spiking became.
span.quote: Thus, theta resonant PYR spiking depends on the effective magnitude of local inhibition.

span.label: Blocking hyperpolarization-activated Ih current with ZD7288 removed the theta-band preference of pyramidal spiking while leaving PV spiking and synaptic transmission intact.
span.quote: Pharmacological blockade of hyperpolarization-activated (I h ) currents abolished theta resonance.

span.label: Pyramidal cells fired at essentially the same theta phase during light-induced PV inhibition as during spontaneous LFP theta, both across the population and cell by cell.
span.quote: The spiking phase of individual PYR during spontaneous LFP theta and during the theta band of chirp-pattern PV activation was similar, both at the population level (LFP theta mean±SEM phase, (π−0.07)±0.17 radians, n=126; chirp phase, (π+0.19)±0.26 radians, n=38; p=0.37, permutation test)

span.label: In the biophysical model, Ih alone gave rebound spiking across all low frequencies; confining it to the theta band required an additional timing element, either an OLM interneuron or synaptic depression of the inhibitory synapse.

span.label: TWO RIVAL MECHANISMS ENUMERATED IN ADVANCE, each named by the filter it would produce: tonic suppression giving a low-pass, or rebound giving a band-pass
span.quote: Theta band-limited discharge of PYR upon PV neuron activation can occur for at least two reasons. First, at high frequencies the high density of spikes emitted by PV cells can tonically suppress their targets, whereas at lower frequencies PYR can still fire in longer windows devoid of strong PV activity, creating in effect a low-pass filter. This scenario is compatible with the frequency filtering properties of inhibitory synapses ( Thomson et al., 2002 ; Markram et al., 2004 ). Second, active properties of pyramidal cells ( Hu et al., 2002 ; Stuart et al., 2007 ) may induce time-locked rebound spiking upon recovery from inhibition ( Llinas et al., 1982 ; Cobb et al., 1995 ) of specific duration, creating in effect a band-pass filter.

span.label: the conclusion the three defences license: periodic inhibition, not inhibition as such, is what creates spiking resonance
span.quote: Thus, while white-noise PV activation was effective in directly inducing frequency-modulated PV spiking and indirectly suppressing PYR spiking, it was ineffective in inducing theta band PYR spiking, suggesting that periodic inhibition is critical for spiking resonance.

span.label: TWO MEASURES BUILT SO EACH EQUALS 1 UNDER ONE RIVAL: frequency correlation is 1 for a purely frequency-dependent unit, time correlation is 1 for a purely adapting one
span.quote: To quantify the frequency/time preference of individual units, we computed, for each cell, two rank correlation coefficients (“frequency correlation” and “time correlation”) between the coherences under the two conditions. For a pure frequency-dependent unit, the coherences during ascending and descending chirps should be identical, and the rank correlation between them (“frequency correlation”) is 1. In contrast, for a pure time-dependent unit the coherences should be mirror images (assuming phase is preserved) and thus the rank correlation between the ascending chirp coherence and the reversed descending chirp coherence is 1.
